questions.question: If one sees some marbles that are immersed in water, he/she will observe them as enlarged. This is because water acts as a:

__
 
• When marbles are immersed in water, they appear enlarged due to the **refraction of light.**
 
• A** convex lens causes light rays to converge,** making objects appear larger.
 
• Water acts as a convex lens, bending light rays inward, creating a magnified image of the marbles.
 
• This effect is due to the convex shape of the water surface around the marbles, which acts like a magnifying glass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with different densities.
 
• It is described by Snell's Law, which relates the angle of incidence to the angle of refraction.

• A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges.
 
• It converges light rays that are parallel to its principal axis.
 
• Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses, cameras, and corrective lenses for hyperopia (farsightedness).
 
 
 
• **Optical Magnification**
 
 
• Optical magnification is the process of enlarging the appearance of an object using lenses or mirrors.
 
• The magnification factor is the ratio of the image size to the actual size of the object.

• Snell's Law formula: n₁ sin(θ₁) = n₂ sin(θ₂), where n₁ and n₂ are the refractive indices of the two media.

questions.question: Suppose a magic mirror is placed in front of a boy. As a result, the boy observes that the image of his head is of the same size, the middle portion of his body is smaller and that of his legs is bigger. Hence, from top to bottom, the magic mirror displays which of the following images?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plane, convex and concave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **A plane mirror** produces images that are of the same size as the object; hence, the boy’s head appears to be of the same size.
 
• A convex mirror diverges light rays and forms smaller images, making the middle portion of the boy’s body appear smaller.
 
• A concave mirror converges light rays and can form magnified images, making the boy’s legs appear larger.
 
• The arrangement of plane, convex, and concave mirrors would create the observed effect from top to bottom.
 
• This specific combination of mirror types is used to create various optical illusions and is common in funhouse mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plane Mirror:**

 
 
• A plane mirror reflects light without changing the image size.
 
• The image is virtual, upright, and laterally inverted.
 
• Commonly used in everyday life, such as in bathrooms and dressing rooms.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors curve outward, causing light rays to diverge.
 
• Produces virtual, diminished, and upright images.
 
• Used in vehicle side mirrors and security mirrors for wider fields of view.
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• Concave mirrors curve inward, causing light rays to converge.
 
• Can produce real, inverted images or virtual, magnified images based on object distance.
 
• Used in applications like shaving mirrors, telescopes, and headlights.
 
 
 
• **Optical Illusions:**
 
 
• Optical illusions are visual phenomena where the perceived image differs from reality.
 
• Utilize various types of mirrors to create exaggerated or distorted images.
 
• Commonly found in amusement parks, funhouses, and art installations.

A and B have undertaken to do a piece of work for ₹800.

questions.question: The average temperature on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday was 32°C, and the average temperature on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday was 36°C. If the temperature on Sunday was 39°C, then find the temperature on Wednesday.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average temperature on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday was 32ºC.

The average temperature on Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday was 36ºC.

Temperature on Sunday = 39ºC

**Formula used:**

Average temperature = Total temperature / Number of days

**Calculation:**

Let M, T, and W be the temperatures on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday respectively.

Average temperature on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday = 32ºC

⇒ (M + T + W) / 3 = 32

⇒ M + T + W = 32 × 3

⇒ M + T + W = 96

Average temperature on Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday = 36ºC

⇒ (S + M + T) / 3 = 36

⇒ 39 + M + T = 36 × 3

⇒ 39 + M + T = 108

⇒ M + T = 69

Now, we know:

M + T + W = 96

M + T = 69

⇒ W = 96 - 69

⇒ W = 27

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Identify the non-biodegradable substance that is generated in a kitchen.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions occurs, - when the exchange of two ions takes place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**double displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a double displacement reaction,** two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds.**
 
• These reactions typically occur in aqueous solutions where ions are free to move.
 
• Double displacement reactions can result in the formation of a precipitate, gas, or weak electrolyte.
 
• An example of a double displacement reaction is the reaction between silver nitrate (AgNO₃) and sodium chloride (NaCl) to form silver chloride (AgCl) and sodium nitrate (NaNO₃).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement Reaction**

 
 
• Involves the replacement of one element in a compound by another element.
 
• Example: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reaction**
 
 
• A single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Example: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
 
 
 
• **Combination Reaction**
 
 
• Two or more substances combine to form a single compound.
 
• Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Precipitate Formation**
 
 
• It occurs when a solid forms from a solution during a chemical reaction.
 
• The solid is called the precipitate.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has three valence electrons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Al (Aluminum)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aluminum (Al)** is the 13th element in the periodic table and belongs to group 13.
 
• It has **three valence electrons** in its outermost shell, which is characteristic of group 13 elements.
 
• Valence electrons in Aluminum play a key role in its chemical reactivity and bonding.
 
• These three valence electrons make Aluminum a trivalent metal, forming compounds like Al₂O₃ (aluminum oxide).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table**

 
 
• The periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number and groups with similar properties.
 
• Group 13 elements include Boron (B), Aluminum (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), and Thallium (Tl).
 
• These elements typically have three electrons in their outermost shell.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons**
 
 
• Valence electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell of an atom.
 
• They are important in determining how an element reacts chemically with other elements.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactivity**
 
 
• Aluminum is a reactive metal, especially at higher temperatures.
 
• It can form compounds with both metals and non-metals.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Aluminum**
 
 
• Due to its light weight, strength, and resistance to corrosion, Aluminum is used in a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, and packaging.

questions.question: In the cases of the Fundamental Rights violations, the Supreme Court of India can be directly petitioned under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court to seek justice when they feel that their Fundamental Rights have been 'unduly deprived'.
 
• This Article is known as the "**Right to Constitutional Remedies**" and it empowers the Supreme Court to issue appropriate orders or writs to enforce Fundamental Rights.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** referred to Article 32 as the "heart and soul of the Constitution" because it provides a guaranteed right to constitutional remedies.
 
• The writs that can be issued under Article 32 include Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 226:** This Article grants similar powers to the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
 
• **Fundamental Rights:** These are a set of rights provided under Part III of the Indian Constitution which include rights such as Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** A writ requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge or into court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.
 
• **Mandamus:** A writ issued as a command to an inferior court or ordering a person to perform a public or statutory duty.
 
• **Certiorari and Prohibition:** These writs are issued to lower courts or tribunals either to transfer a case to a higher authority or to stop proceedings in a case that falls outside their jurisdiction.

questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected across a resistor of resistance R. If a current of 2.4 mA flows through the circuit, then the value of R is _______ ohm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5000 ohms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The voltage (V) across the resistor is given as **12 V.**
 
• The current (I) flowing through the resistor is given as **2.4 mA (milliamperes).**
 
• Ohm's Law states that V = IR, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• Rearranging the formula to find R gives R = V/I.
 
• Substituting the given values: R = 12 V / 2.4 mA = 12 / 0.0024 =** 5000 ohms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• Ohm's Law is a fundamental principle in the field of electrical engineering and physics.
 
• It relates the voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) in an electrical circuit.
 
• The law is typically expressed as V = IR.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement**
 
 
• Voltage is measured in volts (V).
 
• Current is measured in amperes (A), with milliamperes (mA) being 1/1000th of an ampere.
 
• Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).
 
 
 
• **Resistors in Circuits**
 
 
• Resistors are used to control the current flow in electrical circuits.
 
• They are essential components in various electronic devices to ensure proper functionality.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications**
 
 
• Understanding and applying Ohm's Law is crucial for designing and troubleshooting electrical circuits.
 
• It helps in determining the required resistor values to achieve desired current levels in circuits.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first to blend his knowledge of science and mathematics to keep count of individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gregor Johann Mendel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gregor Johann Mendel is known as the **"Father of Genetics"** for his pioneering work in the study of heredity.
 
• He conducted **experiments on pea plants** (Pisum sativum) and formulated the laws of inheritance.
 
• Mendel's work established the fundamental principles of **dominant and recessive traits**.
 
• His research involved meticulous **mathematical analysis** to track the inheritance patterns of specific traits across generations.
 
• Mendel's findings were published in 1866 but were largely unrecognized until the early 20th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendelian Inheritance**

 
 
• Refers to the patterns of inheritance that are characteristic of organisms that reproduce sexually.
 
• It is based on the transmission of genetic information through alleles.
 
• Key concepts include the Law of Segregation and the Law of Independent Assortment.
 
 
 
• **Dominant and Recessive Traits**
 
 
• Dominant traits are those that are expressed in the offspring even when only one allele is present.
 
• Recessive traits require two copies of the same allele to be expressed.
 
 
 
• **Pea Plant Experiments**
 
 
• Mendel chose pea plants for their easily observable traits and ability to self-pollinate.
 
• He studied seven different traits, each with two contrasting forms.
 
• The results of these experiments formed the basis of Mendel's laws.
 
 
 
• **Rediscovery of Mendel's Work**
 
 
• In 1900, three scientists, Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von Tschermak, independently verified Mendel's findings.
 
• This led to the widespread recognition of Mendelian genetics.
 
• Mendel's work laid the groundwork for modern genetics and the study of heredity.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 5 days. They started working together but after 3 days, B left. If the work is completed after 3 more days, B alone could do the entire work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete the work in 5 days.

A and B work together for 3 days.

After B leaves, A completes the remaining work in 3 more days.

**Formula used:**

Work done formula:

 {Total work} = {Efficiency} times {Time} 

Work efficiency of A and B together:

 {Work per day} = (1)/({Total days to complete work)} 

**Calculation:**

Work done by A and B per day:

⇒ (1)/(5) 

Work done by A and B in 3 days:

⇒ 3 times (1)/(5) = (3)/(5) 

Remaining work after B leaves:

⇒ 1 - (3)/(5) = (2)/(5) 

A alone completes this remaining work in 3 days:

⇒ {A's work per day} = (frac{2)/(5)}{3} = (2)/(15) 

Efficiency of A:

⇒ A = (2)/(15) 

Efficiency of A and B together:

⇒ A + B = (1)/(5) 

Efficiency of B:

⇒ B = (1)/(5) - (2)/(15) 

⇒ B = (3)/(15) - (2)/(15) = (1)/(15) 

Time taken by B alone to complete the entire work:

⇒ (1)/(frac{1){15}} = 15 days

**∴ B alone can complete the work in 15 days.**

__
 
• The **first Finance Commission** of India was established in **1951**.
 
• It was constituted under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The primary objective was to define the financial relations between the central government and individual state governments.
 
• **K.C. Neogy **was the first **Chairman** of the Finance Commission.
 
• The commission was tasked with recommending the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between **the Centre and the States.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Article 280 of the Indian Constitution provides for a Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial body.
 
• The President of India appoints the Finance Commission every five years or earlier if necessary.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Finance Commission**
 
 
• To recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Center and the States.
 
• To determine the principles that should govern the grants-in-aid to states by the Center.
 
• To suggest measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and the Municipalities.
 
 
 
• **Composition**
 
 
• The Finance Commission consists of a **Chairman and four other members** appointed by the President of India.
 
• They hold office for the period specified by the **President**.

• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and are** not binding on the government.**

questions.question: The first language which was given the status of a classical language in India is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tamil** was the first language to be declared as a classical language in India.
 
• The Government of India officially granted Tamil the status of classical language in **2004**.
 
• Classical languages are designated based on their ancient history and rich heritage in literature and culture.
 
• As a classical language, Tamil has a long and well-documented history spanning over **2,000 years**.
 
• The classical status helps in promoting and preserving the language's heritage and provides opportunities for academic research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Criteria for Classical Language**

 
 
• High antiquity of its early texts and recorded history over a period of 1500-2000 years.
 
• A body of ancient literature/texts, which is considered a valuable heritage by generations.
 
• The literary tradition should be original and not borrowed from another speech community.
 
• The classical language and literature being distinct from the modern form of the language.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Languages of India**
 
 
• Besides Tamil, other classical languages include Sanskrit, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, and Odia.
 
• Sanskrit was declared as a classical language in 2005.
 
• Kannada and Telugu were both declared in 2008.
 
• Malayalam received the status in 2013, and Odia in 2014.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Classical Language Status**
 
 
• Provision of funds for the development of the language.
 
• Creation of centers of excellence for studies in the classical languages.
 
• Promotion of the language through educational institutions.
 
• Government support for preservation of manuscripts and ancient texts.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of Tamil**
 
 
• Tamil literature is among the oldest in the world, with Sangam literature dating back to the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The language has a rich corpus of classical literature, including the famous epics Silappatikaram and Manimekalai.
 
• Tamil is one of the longest-surviving classical languages in the world.
 
• The language has had a significant impact on the cultural and intellectual history of South India.

questions.question: The coal that we use now comes from plants that lived around _________ years ago
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10,000,000 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The coal we use today was formed from plants that existed around **10 million to 300 million years ago**.
 
• These plants were primarily large ferns, trees, and other vegetation that thrived in swampy environments.
 
• Over millions of years, these plants were buried under layers of water and dirt, compressing them into peat and eventually into coal.
 
• Coal formation is a process that involves the accumulation of plant debris in a swampy environment, followed by burial and compaction.
 
• This process requires millions of years of geological time to transform plant material into coal.

• There are four main types of coal: **anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, and lignite.**
 
• Anthracite has the highest carbon content and energy density, while lignite has the lowest.
 
 
 
• **Coal Formation Stages**
 
 
• The stages of coal formation include peat, lignite, sub-bituminous, bituminous, and anthracite.
 
• Each stage represents a different level of compression and heat applied over millions of years.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Coal**
 
 
• Coal is primarily used as a fuel for electricity generation.
 
• It is also used in the production of steel and cement.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Coal mining and burning contribute to air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact through cleaner coal technologies and alternative energy sources.

questions.question: The line joining the two focii of a lens is called ________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Principal Axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The principal axis is an imaginary line that passes through the center of curvature and the optical center of a lens or mirror.**
 
• It is the main axis of symmetry for the lens or mirror, and it helps in defining the focal points.
 
• In a lens, the principal axis intersects the lens at the optical center, which is the midpoint of the lens.
 
• Light rays parallel to the principal axis converge (in a convex lens) or appear to diverge (in a concave lens) at the focal point on the principal axis.
 
• The principal axis is crucial for understanding the formation of images by lenses and mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Focal Point**

 
 
• The point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after passing through a lens or reflecting from a mirror.
 
• In a convex lens, it is real and in front of the lens; in a concave lens, it is virtual and behind the lens.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**
 
 
• The distance between the lens or mirror and its focal point.
 
• It is a measure of how strongly the lens or mirror converges or diverges light.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature**
 
 
• The radius of the sphere from which a spherical mirror or lens surface is a segment.
 
• It is twice the focal length for mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Optical Center**
 
 
• The point on the principal axis of a lens where light passes through without being deviated.
 
• It is the geometric center of a lens.

• The blue-black color in the iodine test is specifically due to the amylose component.

• Iodine solution is typically made by dissolving iodine in potassium iodide solution.
 
• It is used as a reagent to detect the presence of starch.
 
• The solution is usually brownish-red but turns blue-black in the presence of starch.
 
 
 
• **Rice Flour:**

questions.question: Macroeconomics can be defined as:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Macroeconomics** focuses on aggregate indicators such as **GDP, unemployment rates, and inflation.**
 
• It examines the economy-wide phenomena and policies that affect the economic performance of a country.
 
• Key areas of study include national income, output, consumption, investment, savings, and overall economic growth.
 
• Macroeconomics provides a comprehensive overview of how the economy operates as a whole, rather than individual markets.
 
• This field of economics plays a vital role in formulating governmental policies to stabilize and grow the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Newlands arranged the then known elements in the order of _________ .
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• John Newlands, an English chemist, proposed the** Law of Octaves in 1864,** arranging elements in** increasing atomic masses.**
 
• He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first element, creating a periodic pattern.
 
• Newlands' arrangement was one of the earliest attempts to classify elements based on their properties and relative atomic mass.
 
• This arrangement led to the development of the modern periodic table, although Newlands' work was initially met with skepticism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendeleev's Periodic Table**

 
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev improved upon Newlands' work by arranging elements in order of increasing atomic mass but also by their chemical properties.
 
• Mendeleev's table left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties accurately.
 
• This table eventually evolved into the modern periodic table where elements are arranged by increasing atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Moseley's Contribution**
 
 
• Henry Moseley, in 1913, redefined the periodic table by arranging elements by increasing atomic number, not atomic mass.
 
• This resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev's table and provided a more accurate organization of the elements.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Law**
 
 
• The Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
 
• This means elements with similar properties recur at regular intervals when arranged by atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table**
 
 
• The modern periodic table is structured in periods (rows) and groups (columns) based on atomic number.
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.

46² = 1156 + 2ab

2116 = 1156 + 2ab

questions.question: Which of the following compounds of carbon does NOT exist?

The correct answer is __**CH6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CH6** does not exist because it is not possible to have six hydrogen atoms bonded to a single carbon atom under normal conditions.
 
• The carbon atom can form a maximum of four covalent bonds due to its tetravalency, adhering to the octet rule.
 
• Common carbon compounds include **CH4 (methane)**, **C2H6 (ethane)**, and **C6H6 (benzene)**, all of which follow the valency rules of carbon.
 
• In the case of **CH4**, carbon forms four single bonds with hydrogen atoms, while in **C2H6**, each carbon atom forms three single bonds with hydrogen and one single bond with another carbon atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Octet Rule**

 
 
• A chemical rule of thumb that reflects the observation that atoms of main-group elements tend to combine in such a way that each atom has eight electrons in its valence shell.
 
• This rule is a guiding principle for understanding the bonding behavior of atoms.
 
 
 
• **Tetravalency of Carbon**
 
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons and thus can form four covalent bonds with other atoms.
 
• This property allows carbon to form a wide variety of complex organic molecules.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Structures**
 
 
• The structure of a molecule is determined by the arrangement of its atoms and the bonds between them.
 
• Methane (CH4) has a tetrahedral structure, while benzene (C6H6) has a planar hexagonal structure with alternating double bonds.
 
 
 
• **Hybridization**
 
 
• The concept of mixing atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals suitable for the pairing of electrons to form chemical bonds.
 
• For example, in methane (CH4), carbon undergoes sp3 hybridization to form four equivalent bonds with hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: Normally, in a healthy adult, the initial filtrate in the kidneys is about _________ daily.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**180 L**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The initial filtrate in the kidneys of a healthy adult is about **180 liters daily**.
 
• This filtrate consists of water, glucose, salts, and waste products from the blood.
 
• Approximately **99% of this filtrate is reabsorbed** back into the bloodstream.
 
• The remaining 1% forms urine, which is excreted from the body.
 
• This process is crucial for maintaining the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nephron**

 
 
• The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney responsible for the formation of urine.
 
• Each kidney contains about 1 million nephrons.
 
• Nephrons filter blood, reabsorb needed substances, and excrete waste as urine.
 
 
 
• **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)**
 
 
• GFR is the rate at which the blood is filtered in the kidneys.
 
• It is a measure of kidney function, with a normal GFR being around 90-120 mL/min.
 
• Decreased GFR may indicate kidney disease.
 
 
 
• **Reabsorption in Kidneys**
 
 
• Reabsorption involves the movement of water and solutes back into the bloodstream.
 
• It primarily occurs in the renal tubules of the nephron.
 
• Essential substances like glucose, amino acids, and ions are selectively reabsorbed.
 
 
 
• **Urine Formation**
 
 
• Urine formation involves three main processes: filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.
 
• The final urine is composed of water, urea, creatinine, and other waste products.
 
• On average, a healthy adult excretes about 1-2 liters of urine daily.

questions.question: Let n be the least number which when divided by 15, 18, 20 and 27, the remainder in each case is 3 and n is divisible by 53. What is the sum of the digits of n?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

n is the least number which when divided by 15, 18, 20, and 27 leaves a remainder of 3 and is divisible by 53.

**Formula used:**

The least number n can be expressed as:

n = LCM(15, 18, 20, 27) + 3, and n must be divisible by 53.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Find LCM of 15, 18, 20, and 27:

⇒ Prime factorization:

15 = (3 × 5), 18 = (2 × 3²), 20 = (2² × 5), 27 = (3³)

⇒ LCM = (2² × 3³ × 5 = 540)

⇒ (n = 540 + 3 = 543)

⇒ Check divisibility by 53:

(543 ÷ 53 = 10.245...) (Not divisible)

⇒ Add multiples of 540 to ensure divisibility by 53:

(543 + 540 × 1 = 1083)

(1083 ÷ 53 = 20.43...) (Not divisible)

(543 + 540 × 2 = 1623)

(1623 ÷ 53 = 30.6) (Not Divisible)

(543 + 540 × 3 = 2163)

(2163 ÷ 53 = 40.8) (Not Divisible)

(543 + 540 × 4 = 2703)

(2703 ÷ 53 = 51) (Divisible)

⇒ Sum of digits of (n = 2703):

(2 + 7 + 0 + 3 = 12)

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The resistance of a material is inversely proportional to the length of the wire.
The resistance of a material is directly proportional to the radius of the wire.
The resistance of a material is directly proportional to the area of cross section.
The resistance of a material is directly proportional to its length.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The resistance of a material is directly proportional to its length.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Resistance (R)** of a material is given by the **formula R = ρ(L/A)**, where ρ is the resistivity, L is the length, and A is the cross-sectional area.
 
• The resistance of a wire is **directly proportional to its length (L)**; as the length increases, the resistance increases.
 
• This relationship is crucial in designing electrical circuits and components to ensure proper functionality and safety.
 
• In practical applications, longer wires are used with higher resistance to control the current flow, ensuring that devices operate within safe limits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistivity (ρ)**: This is a material property that indicates how much the material opposes the flow of electric current. It is measured in ohm-meters (Ω·m).
 
• **Cross-Sectional Area (A)**: The area of the wire's cross-section perpendicular to its length. Resistance is inversely proportional to this area; as the area increases, the resistance decreases.
 
• **Ohm's Law**: A fundamental principle in electronics stating that the current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance (R). Expressed as V = IR.
 
• **Conductivity**: The reciprocal of resistivity, it measures a material's ability to conduct electric current. High conductivity materials have low resistivity and vice versa.
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance**: In addition to length and cross-sectional area, the resistance of a material can be affected by its temperature, with most materials having higher resistance at higher temperatures.

questions.question: Our body works within the pH range of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7 to 7.8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The normal pH range of the human body is tightly regulated between **7.35 and 7.45**.
 
• This pH range is considered slightly alkaline and is essential for the proper functioning of biochemical processes.
 
• A pH below 7.35 indicates a condition called **acidosis**, while a pH above 7.45 indicates **alkalosis**.
 
• Maintaining this pH range is crucial for the body's enzyme activity and metabolic processes.
 
• The kidneys and lungs play a significant role in regulating the body’s pH balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acidosis**

 
 
• Acidosis is a condition where the body’s pH falls below 7.35.
 
• It can result from increased acid production, decreased acid excretion, or a loss of bicarbonate.
 
• Symptoms may include fatigue, confusion, and shortness of breath.
 
 
 
• **Alkalosis**
 
 
• Alkalosis occurs when the body’s pH rises above 7.45.
 
• It can be caused by a loss of acid or an excess of bicarbonate.
 
• Symptoms may include muscle twitching, hand tremor, and light-headedness.
 
 
 
• **Buffer Systems**
 
 
• Buffer systems in the body, such as the bicarbonate buffer system, help maintain pH balance.
 
• These systems neutralize excess acids or bases to prevent drastic changes in pH.
 
 
 
• **Role of Kidneys and Lungs**
 
 
• The kidneys regulate pH by excreting hydrogen ions and reabsorbing bicarbonate from urine.
 
• The lungs regulate pH by controlling the levels of carbon dioxide through breathing.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sexually transmitted viral disease?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome)** is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
 
• It is a sexually transmitted infection that can also be spread through contact with infected blood, from mother to child during pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding.
 
• HIV attacks and weakens the body's immune system, making the individual more susceptible to infections and certain cancers.
 
• There is currently no cure for AIDS, but antiretroviral therapy (ART) can manage and control the virus, improving the quality of life for those infected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)**

 
 
• HIV is a retrovirus that primarily infects components of the human immune system such as CD4+ T cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells.
 
• Without treatment, HIV infection progresses in stages, starting with acute infection, then clinical latency, and finally, AIDS.
 
 
 
• **Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)**
 
 
• ART involves taking a combination of HIV medicines (called an HIV treatment regimen) every day.
 
• ART helps reduce the viral load in the blood, maintain immune system function, and prevent onward transmission of the virus.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of HIV/AIDS**
 
 
• Practicing safe sex by using condoms.
 
• Regular HIV testing and counseling.
 
• Using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for those at high risk.
 
• Avoiding sharing needles or syringes.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact**
 
 
• According to UNAIDS, in 2020, there were approximately 37.7 million people living with HIV worldwide.
 
• Sub-Saharan Africa remains the most severely affected region, with nearly 1 in every 25 adults (3.6%) living with HIV.

questions.question: When the MP is positive but declining, it means __________

options.text: TP increases at a constant rate
TP increases at a decreasing rate
TP increases at an increasing rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TP increases at a decreasing rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **When Marginal Product (MP) is positive but declining, Total Product (TP) continues to increase but at a decreasing rate.**
 
• This indicates that each additional unit of input contributes less to the total output than the previous unit.
 
• The phenomenon is often observed in the phase of diminishing returns in production processes.
 
• It reflects the point where the efficiency of additional inputs starts to fall, though they still contribute positively to the overall output.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Product (MP):**

 
 
• Marginal Product is the additional output produced by adding one more unit of a specific input, keeping other inputs constant.
 
• It is a key concept in the study of production and efficiency in economics.
 
• When MP is positive but declining, it suggests diminishing marginal returns.
 
 
 
• **Total Product (TP):**
 
 
• Total Product represents the total quantity of output produced with a given quantity of inputs.
 
• It is a cumulative measure of the production process efficiency.
 
• TP increases initially at an increasing rate, then at a decreasing rate, and eventually may decline.
 
 
 
• **Diminishing Returns:**
 
 
• The law of diminishing returns states that as more of a variable input is added to a fixed input, the additional output produced from each additional unit of the variable input eventually decreases.
 
• This principle is crucial in resource allocation and production planning.
 
 
 
• **Production Function:**
 
 
• A production function illustrates the relationship between inputs used in production and the resulting output.
 
• It helps in understanding the efficiency and productivity of different input combinations.

questions.question: The quantity of a commodity that a consumer is willing to buy and is able to afford, given prices of goods and consumers' tastes and preferences is called _________ for the commodity.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Demand** refers to the quantity of a commodity that consumers are willing and able to purchase at various price levels during a given period.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in economics that describes a consumer's desire and ability to pay for goods or services.
 
• Demand is influenced by factors such as **price, income, tastes, preferences, and prices of related goods**.
 
• The **Law of Demand** states that, all else being equal, an increase in the price of a good will decrease the quantity demanded, and vice versa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Price Elasticity of Demand**

 
 
• It measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded of a good to a change in its price.
 
• Goods can be elastic (responsive to price changes) or inelastic (less responsive to price changes).
 
 
 
• **Income Elasticity of Demand**
 
 
• It measures the responsiveness of demand to a change in consumer income.
 
• Normal goods have a positive income elasticity, while inferior goods have a negative income elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Cross Elasticity of Demand**
 
 
• It measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded for one good when the price of another good changes.
 
• Substitutes have a positive cross elasticity, while complements have a negative cross elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Determinants of Demand**
 
 
• Factors such as consumer preferences, population size, consumer incomes, prices of related goods, and future expectations about prices and income.
 
• Understanding these determinants helps businesses and policymakers make informed decisions.

Suppose an electric iron when connected to a 220 V source draws the same current as that of the three appliances in the above, then the resistance and current flowing through the iron are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30.77 Ω and 7.15 A, respectively**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Given an electric lamp, a toaster, and a water filter with resistances of 40 Ω, 200 Ω, and 400 Ω respectively are connected in parallel.
 
• The equivalent resistance (Rₑq) of these resistors in parallel is calculated using the formula:

 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃.
 
• **Applying the formula**: 1/Rₑq = 1/40 + 1/200 + 1/400 = (10+2.5+1.25)/400 = 13.75/400, Rₑq = 400/13.75 ≈ 29.09 Ω.
 
• The total current (I) drawn from the source is I = V/Rₑq = 220 V / 29.09 Ω ≈ 7.57 A.
 
• An electric iron drawing the same current (7.57 A) from a 220 V source has a resistance R = V/I = 220 V / 7.57 A ≈ 29.07 Ω, which matches closely with option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit**
 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each component is the same, while the total current is the sum of the currents through each component.
 
• The reciprocal of the total resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
 
 
• **Power Consumption**
 
 
• Power consumed by an electrical device is given by P = VI, where P is power, V is voltage, and I is current.
 
• In a resistive circuit, power can also be calculated using P = I²R or P = V²/R.
 
 
 
• **Resistance and Conductance**
 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of current in a conductor, while conductance is the measure of the ease with which current flows.
 
• Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance, G = 1/R, and is measured in Siemens (S).

• Using condoms correctly every time during vaginal, anal, or oral sex is crucial for effective protection.

• **Other Contraceptive Methods**
 
 
• Copper T (Intrauterine Device) and oral contraceptives are primarily used to prevent pregnancy.
 
• These methods do not offer protection against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections.
 
 
 
• **Dual Protection**
 
 
• Using condoms along with another contraceptive method (e.g., oral contraceptives) provides protection against both unintended pregnancies and STIs.
 
• This practice is known as dual protection and is recommended for sexually active individuals.
